what-is-codex: A person at a desk hands a neat task card to a friendly abstract AI agent (a glowing rounded robot-like assistant, not humanoid), the agent then works across an open laptop with a code editor, a stack of documents and a small terminal window, small checkmarks appearing as steps complete. Conveys delegating a real task to a capable assistant.
agent-basics: Split composition. Left half: a simple chat bubble exchange, one question bubble and one answer bubble, static and flat. Right half: the same assistant now actively working in a loop: reading a folder of files, using a wrench tool, looking at results through a magnifier, adjusting, arranged as a circular loop of four small stations with arrows. Conveys the difference between answering and acting.
context-layers: Three translucent stacked layers floating above each other, feeding light down into a small assistant at the bottom: the top layer holds a rulebook and gear (project rules), the middle layer holds a few highlighted files and folders (selected files), the bottom layer holds a short thread of conversation bubbles. Some irrelevant clutter (crumpled papers) is filtered out to the side by a soft funnel. Conveys giving the right context and filtering noise.
sandbox-and-approval: A small assistant works inside a transparent glass workshop box on a desk, with its tools and files inside the box. At the edge of the box there is a gate with a small approval button, and a human hand outside is about to press approve on a request card held up by the assistant. Network cables outside the box are neatly unplugged with a lock icon shape. Conveys sandbox boundaries and human approval.
local-vs-cloud: Split scene connected by a gentle dotted path. Left: a cozy local workstation, a laptop on a desk with a small assistant working right next to the user. Right: a calm cloud platform floating above, with several identical isolated container boxes each holding a small assistant working in parallel, results flowing back down to the laptop as small parcels. Conveys local versus cloud execution.
verification: A large magnifying glass hovering over a document showing a code diff with green and red highlighted lines, next to it a checklist clipboard with some items checked and one item flagged, and a small test tube rack with green lights. A person calmly reviews. Conveys verifying results before accepting them.
task-brief: A clean blueprint style task card being assembled from four distinct pieces snapping together like puzzle tiles: a target (goal), a folder (context), a fence segment (constraints), and a checkmark badge (definition of done). An assistant receives the completed card with confidence. Conveys writing a clear, complete task.
skills-toolkit: A successful workflow (a short row of glowing step cards ending in a green check) is packed into an open rounded toolbox with labeled-by-shape compartments: a stack of instruction cards, a gear, a wrench, a small template page. The toolbox is then copied into several identical toolboxes handed to several small friendly white round robot assistants. Conveys packaging a proven workflow as a reusable Skill shared with many agents.
cases-deliverables: A bright workshop table showing finished tangible deliverables laid out side by side: a printed weekly report with a small bar chart, a typeset article page, a slide deck fanned out, a laptop showing a simple web page, and a code file with a green checkmark. Each item has a small blank tag. Conveys hands-on practice that ends with real results.
handoff-and-resume: Relay handoff scene: one small assistant passes a neatly organized notebook and a progress bar card to a second assistant across a desk, with a calendar page turning in the background and a bookmark placed in a half-finished task board. Conveys handing off work and resuming later without losing progress.
learning-paths: An illustrated map with four distinct winding paths starting from the same open book at the bottom: one path for a beginner with a small flag, one for a creator with a pen and paper, one for a developer with a laptop and brackets shape, one for a team with several small figures together. Paths lead upward to a summit with a checkmark. Conveys choosing a learning path by role.
team-guardrails: A small team of diverse people around a table collaborating with several small assistants, surrounded by soft protective guardrails and a shield shape, a shared rulebook in the middle, and a review station where a person signs off on work. Conveys team adoption with governance and safety.
home-weekly-report: A messy spreadsheet grid on the left with a few rows highlighted (duplicates struck through, a refund row marked), transforming via a glowing arrow into a clean one-page weekly report on the right with a bar chart, a small line trend and a reconciliation checklist with green checks. Close-up, centered composition, simple and iconic.
home-bug-fix: A code editor panel with a failing test indicator glowing red, a small bug creature being gently lifted out with tweezers, and the same test indicator turning green on a second panel, connected by a small wrench. Close-up, centered composition, simple and iconic.
home-article: Three source documents of different colors on the left (one with a highlighted quote, one with a small table, one with a date stamp) with thin connecting threads leading into a neatly typeset article page on the right that has footnote markers and a small fact table. Close-up, centered composition, simple and iconic.
home-path-beginner: A friendly beginner sitting with a laptop showing a single simple card, a small assistant beside them, a safety helmet shape and three stepping stones in front leading forward, a small green check on the first stone. Simple, iconic, centered.
home-path-creator: A creator at a desk with a stack of source notes, an article page and a fanned set of presentation slides emerging from them, a pen and a small assistant helping arrange the slides. Simple, iconic, centered.
home-path-developer: A developer at a desk with two monitors: one showing code with a highlighted line, the other showing test results with green bars, a small assistant pointing at the diff, a handoff notebook on the desk. Simple, iconic, centered.
home-path-team: A small team of three people around a table with a shared calendar showing a two-week plan, a checklist board and a few small assistants, one person holding a rollback arrow shaped badge. Simple, iconic, centered.
start-here: A trailhead at the edge of a calm landscape with a large signpost of blank arrow boards pointing to several paths, an open guidebook on a stand, a small friendly assistant waving the reader in. Conveys a welcoming starting point.
getting-started: A short sequence of four stepping platforms rising left to right: a laptop being set up, a key card for signing in, a small project folder, and a first task card with a green check at the top platform. A small assistant walks along with a person. Conveys a quick setup path.
undo-and-recover: A file document being restored: a translucent rewind arrow circles around a stack of version snapshots, one older snapshot glows and slides back into place, a safety net below catches a crumpled page. Conveys undo and recovery.
permissions-approvals: A row of four doors or gates with different lock levels: an open door for reading files, a door with a small key for writing, a door with a switch for running commands, a door with a globe shape for network access. A person holds a ring of keys and decides which to hand to a small assistant. Conveys permission levels.
tokens-compaction: A long unrolled scroll of conversation bubbles flowing into a press machine that compacts it into a small neat summary card, which then fits snugly into a limited window frame with room to spare. Conveys context limits and compaction.
threads-tasks-projects: Nested containers: a large project box contains several task folders, each task folder contains a few thread strands of conversation bubbles, arranged clearly like a cutaway diagram, a small assistant organizing them. Conveys how projects, tasks, and threads nest.
desktop-app: A calm desktop control center on a large monitor: several task cards in columns with progress rings, one card expanded showing a side-by-side diff with green and red lines, an approval toggle, a small assistant busy in each lane. Conveys managing parallel local tasks in a desktop app.
cli: A large terminal window with a dark pane and glowing prompt cursor, blocks of abstract command lines (no readable text) and a small assistant sitting on top of the terminal frame typing on a mini keyboard, with pipes connecting to a script scroll and a test tube. Conveys working in the command line.
ide: A code editor with a file tree on the left, a highlighted code selection in the middle, and a side panel where a small assistant suggests an inline change with a small accept button. Conveys an assistant inside the editor.
web-and-cloud: A web browser window showing a repository card connected by a dotted line up to a cloud with isolated container boxes running tasks, finished results returning as a pull request shaped card with a green check. Conveys delegating tasks to the cloud from the web.
tools-overview: A neat tool belt laid out on a table: a terminal window badge, a browser window badge, a magnifier for search, an image frame, a microphone, and a cursor pointer for computer use, with a small assistant choosing the right one. Conveys choosing tools.
files-and-artifacts: A conveyor loop passing by a small assistant: different file types ride on it as distinct shapes, a code file with brackets, an image frame, a PDF booklet, a spreadsheet grid, a slide deck, each getting a small inspection check. Conveys handling many file types and checking outputs.
agent-planning: A small assistant drawing a step-by-step plan on a whiteboard as a vertical sequence of numbered-looking blank boxes connected by arrows, while a person points at one step to adjust it before work begins. Conveys planning before execution.
agents-md: A repository folder tree in cutaway: a thick guidebook sits at the root folder, smaller note cards are pinned in nested subfolders, and a small assistant reads the guidebook first, then the nearest note card. Conveys project instruction files and scope.
prompt-injection: A document and a web page float toward a small assistant; hidden inside the web page a tiny sneaky note with a red tint is caught by a translucent shield filter, while the clean content passes through. Conveys defending against prompt injection.
mcp-overview: A small friendly white round robot assistant plugs into a central hub adapter with a standard universal connector; cables run from the hub to a database cylinder, a calendar, a ticket kanban board and a cloud drive. All connectors look identical and standardized. Conveys MCP as a unified connector between assistant and external tools.
plugins-overview: A ribbon-tied extension package slides along a glowing rail toward several workstations. At one workstation the package is being unwrapped and plugged into a slot, at another a package is cleanly removed and leaves a tidy empty slot. Small white round robot assistant watches. Conveys installing and cleanly uninstalling plugin bundles.
prompt-debugging: A person compares two output cards side by side on a workbench: the left output misses a target board, the right hits the center; between them a task card is being adjusted with a small screwdriver and a magnifier. Conveys diagnosing and improving a prompt.
long-running-tasks: A long winding road with checkpoint flags at intervals and a progress bar banner above, a small assistant carrying a backpack walks the road, a person at a checkpoint holds a signpost to steer direction. Conveys long tasks with checkpoints and steering.
failure-recovery: A small block tower that partially toppled is calmly being rebuilt by a person and a small assistant following a checklist, a rollback arrow returning a block to a stable base, a first aid style kit nearby. Conveys recovering from failures methodically.
pets-hero: A tiny friendly pixel-art style desktop companion creature (a small round cat-like blob with big eyes) sitting happily on the edge of a floating code editor window, cheering softly. The window shows abstract code lines. Small sparkles and a little status light around. Conveys a cute animated companion living inside the Codex client, purely decorative, not a program.
pets-anatomy: An open cardboard-like rounded package box on a desk, from which three items float up and are neatly arranged: a small JSON-like config card with a name tag, a wide sprite sheet grid card showing many tiny frames of the same cute round creature in different poses, and a small license scroll with a seal. Conveys a pet being a small local resource bundle of metadata, animation sheet and license.
pets-install: A person's hand carefully places a small labeled folder package into a drawer of a tidy cabinet in the shape of a desk file organizer, a magnifying glass inspects the package first, a small shield with a check mark floats nearby, then a small refresh arrow circles near a laptop screen where a cute round companion creature appears. Conveys inspecting then copying a local resource into place and refreshing.
pets-spritesheet: A wide sprite sheet grid of the same cute round creature in a regular grid of rows and columns, each row a different action: idle, working, waiting, celebrating, error. Next to the sheet a single frame is highlighted by a glowing square frame and a small filmstrip arrow leads to a screen playing the animation. Conveys cutting frames from one sheet and playing them in sequence.
pets-create: A creator's desk: a drawing tablet with a sketch of a cute round creature, a color palette, a ruler laying out a grid, a transparent checkerboard background swatch, and a finished sprite sheet card being slid into a package folder. Conveys the workflow of making a pet from artwork to a loadable package.
skills-anatomy: A cutaway isometric view of a folder opened like a layered cabinet: a prominent main instruction card on top, and under it three labeled-by-icon compartments: a stack of reference documents, a set of template pages, and a small gear with script scroll. Thin glowing lines show the assistant loading only the compartment it needs. Conveys the layered structure of a Skill and on-demand loading.
skills-first-skill: A small friendly white round robot assistant builds its first Skill like assembling a kit on a workbench: it places an instruction card into a folder, a magnifier checks a code diff page with red and green lines, a checklist is ticked, and a finished folder gets a small flag. Conveys creating a first pr-review style skill step by step.
skills-when: A decision scene: a conveyor belt carries different task cards toward a signpost with two branches. Repetitive, well-defined, multi-step tasks go left into a reusable toolbox bin with a green glow; one-off, vague tasks go right into a plain chat bubble bin. A small white round robot assistant stands at the fork. Conveys judging which tasks are worth packaging as Skills.
skills-trigger: Two ways of calling a skill shown side by side. Left: a hand points directly at one specific toolbox card and a speech bubble with a dollar-sign-shaped tag appears (explicit call). Right: the assistant reads a description label on several closed toolboxes and picks the matching one by itself, with a soft glow (implicit trigger). Conveys explicit versus implicit skill triggering and the role of the description.
skills-scripts: A small white round robot assistant hands a repetitive step to a neat mechanical machine (a deterministic script box with gears and a conveyor), whose output passes under a test checkpoint with green check lights and one red light being fixed. Conveys deterministic scripts inside a skill and verifying them with tests.
skills-security: A skill package arrives on a delivery belt and is inspected before installation: a magnifying glass over the package, a shield with a check, a padlock on a permission gate, and a version rollback arrow looping back to an earlier package on a shelf. A small white round robot assistant waits calmly behind a gate. Conveys source checks, permission boundaries, upgrades and rollback.
mcp-connect: Step by step on a desk: a small white round robot assistant inserts a connector plug into a server box, a key and login window (OAuth feel, no text) hands over a token, then a green status light turns on and a test prompt bubble sends a request through the cable to a database and receives a result. Conveys connecting, authorizing and verifying the first MCP server.
mcp-debugging: A four-layer transparent stack like a cross section: bottom configuration file card, transport pipe, authentication key, top tool panel. A small white round robot assistant with a flashlight and magnifier inspects layer by layer, one layer shows a red broken pipe segment being repaired with a green glow. Conveys layered troubleshooting of an MCP connection.
hooks-guardrail: A glowing gate placed across the path of a tool call: a small robot arm carrying a command card approaches the gate, a guard checkpoint scanner reads it, a green lane lets safe commands through and a red barrier stops a dangerous one with a clear shield. A small test panel with green lights sits beside it. Conveys a PreToolUse guardrail that blocks risky actions and is tested.
automations-schedule: A big friendly clock and calendar above a looping conveyor: a verified task card travels around the loop on a schedule, producing a small result report each cycle, and a human reviewer at a desk glances at the report with a thumbs-up and can press a pause button. A small white round robot assistant works the loop. Conveys scheduled recurring tasks with human review.
skills-capability-ladder: A rising isometric staircase of six glowing steps climbing from lower left to upper right. Step 1: a single sticky note with a speech bubble (one prompt). Step 2: an instruction folder card with a template page (a Skill). Step 3: two small white round robot assistants working side by side (subagents). Step 4: a standard plug connector joined to a cloud and a database (MCP). Step 5: a small glowing gate with a shield (a Hook guardrail). Step 6 at the top: a ribbon-tied package handed to a group of teammates beside a clock and calendar (plugin distribution and scheduled automation). A friendly white round robot assistant mascot stands at the bottom pointing upward. Conveys growing from one prompt to a team capability pack.
roadmap-ai-application: A long winding isometric road climbing through six glowing milestone platforms from the lower left to the upper right, each platform with a different symbolic object in order: a small book and library shelf (knowledge grounding), a chat window with a control dial (input control), a universal plug connector (tool protocol), two small robot assistants working together (coordinated execution), a toolbox folder (reusable skills), and at the top a sturdy scaffold frame with checkmarks, gauges and a safety net around a small robot (verifiable harness). A friendly white round robot assistant mascot walks along the road. Conveys the evolution of AI application engineering over time.
flow-bug-fix: A five-station left-to-right assembly path for fixing a bug safely. Station 1: a test tube rack with a red light failing (reproduce, red). Station 2: a magnifier tracing a root cause to a single glowing line of code. Station 3: a tiny precise screwdriver making a minimal fix on a small part. Station 4: the same test tubes now green (green). Station 5: a regression checklist, a diff page and a green shield stamp on a delivery box. A thin evidence ribbon runs underneath connecting all stations. A white round robot assistant guides the path. Conveys red then green then regression with an evidence trail.
flow-subagents: A main white round robot assistant at the center of a command table holding a plan board with goal, constraints and permissions icons. Three small white robot assistants in separate transparent glass pods (independent contexts), each carrying a different tool (a code map with magnifier, a test tube with a log scroll, a comparison scale with a risk flag) work in parallel and return glowing evidence cards back into the main robot's tray for final acceptance. Dotted boundary lines show a shared workspace floor beneath all pods with a small lock marking write ownership. Conveys main agent orchestrating focused subagents and evidence returning for review.
flow-client-selection: A signpost fork in front of one central question mark-free decision plaza: a friendly white robot assistant stands at the center asking where the work happens. Four glowing paths lead to four distinct places: a desktop app window with a task list and diff view, a terminal window with a prompt cursor, a code editor window with an open file and selection highlight, and a cloud platform with isolated container boxes working in parallel. Conveys choosing the Codex entry point by where the work happens.
flow-sandbox-approval: A glass sandbox workshop box with a visible boundary line. Inside, a small white robot assistant works freely on files and a terminal. At the edge, an action card tries to cross the boundary and meets a gate keeper desk with two lanes: a human hand pressing a green approve button which opens the gate narrowly for one specific item, and a red decline lane where the robot narrows its request and picks a safer in-box path. Below the whole scene a final verification strip with a diff page, test lights and a checklist. Conveys sandbox limits scope, approval asks before crossing, verification confirms result.
flow-task-loop: A closed loop track in isometric style: a task card (made of four colored tiles for goal, context, constraints and acceptance) enters a first station of exploration with a magnifier, then planning with a step list, then execution with small tools, then verification with test lights and a diff page. A green check lets the result exit as a delivery box with an evidence stamp; a red return arrow carries failure evidence back to the beginning. A white round robot assistant moves along the loop. Conveys a prompt that closes the loop through execution, evidence and feedback.
flow-scheduled-safety: Five stepping stones along a gentle curve from left to right: 1 a durable task card with stop-condition flags, 2 a manual dry run with a clipboard and green check, 3 a context choice between a fresh blank page and a continuing thread, 4 a materials shelf with a cloud upload and a local project folder, 5 an unattended run inside a small sandbox glass box with a clock, ending at an inbox tray where a human reviewer checks results with a pause button. A white round robot assistant walks the stones. Conveys going from manual verification to safe scheduled runs.
arch-work-system: A cutaway isometric architecture scene. Top row: three entry cards feeding in from above: a task prompt note, a rulebook labeled by a gear and book shape (project rules), and a toolbox folder (Skill), plus a clock calendar on the side (scheduled task). Center: a large glass box showing one task run with a main white robot assistant coordinating two small subagent robots and a plugged connector to cloud, files and database (tools). Around the glass box a thin glowing guardrail frame with check gates (hooks) at the entrance and exit. Bottom: a plugin package with a ribbon being handed to a team. Conveys the cooperating parts of a reusable Codex work system.
map-extension-selection: A decision garden map seen from above in isometric style: a friendly white robot assistant stands at a central round plaza holding a question card; paths branch to six small themed islands: a rulebook book (always-on project rules), a toolbox folder (reusable skill), a plug and cloud (external connector), a guard gate (hook), two small robots side by side (subagents), and a ribbon package plus clock (plugin and scheduled task). Paths are labeled only by icons. Conveys choosing an extension mechanism by what needs to be persisted.
flow-hook-lifecycle: A horizontal timeline track shaped like a ribbon with glowing checkpoint gates in order: a start flag (session start), a prompt note gate, a pre-tool shield gate before a tool execution machine with a small tool icon, a permission handshake gate, a post-tool inspection gate with a magnifier after the machine, a compression gate with a squeeze press, and a stop sign gate at the end. Underneath a smaller branch track carries two tiny robot subagents with their own start and end gates. A white round robot assistant rides the main track. Conveys the lifecycle events where hooks can intervene before or after side effects.
